input.title: chat: summarize Agent Merge turns in the prompt timeline
input.body:
## Description

Agent Merge drives its repair turns with a machine-facing `<agent_merge_state>` block. The prompt timeline (the chat "mini map") previews each prompt with its first non-empty line, so every merge turn showed up in the gutter rail, ruler hover card and sticky header as a bare `<agent_merge_state>` tag.

### Changes

- **`promptTimelineModel.ts`** — previews a request with `getAgentMergeRequestLabel()`, falling back to the message text. This is the same localized summary the transcript renders in place of the state block, and the same helper `chatFindModel` and `chatAccessibilityProvider` already use. All rails derive from `PromptTimelineModel`, so one change covers the dot list, ruler, hover card, sticky header and the ticks' `ariaLabel`.

  ```ts
  private _requestPreview(item: IChatRequestViewModel): string {
      // …
      const preview = getPromptPreview(getAgentMergeRequestLabel(item) ?? messageText);
      // …
  }
  ```

- **Preview memoization** — keyed on the prompt's text, cleared with the sibling signal cache on rebind. `_recompute()` runs on every streamed token, and recognizing a merge turn means parsing its whole state block: ~29 µs for a realistic 10 KB prompt versus ~3 µs for the plain preview.

- **Test** — builds a real prompt with `buildAgentMergePrompt` and asserts the tick reads `Agent Merge, 1 comment, 1 check failing`.

### Notes for review

Two alternatives were considered and not taken:

- **Excluding merge turns from the timeline** (matching live sessions, where `isSystemInitiated` filters them out). These turns only reach the timeline in *restored* sessions, where the transcript renders them as a full raw user bubble — hiding them would leave a large visible turn with no rail entry and make the sticky header name the wrong prompt. Relabelling also degrades gracefully if a human ever pastes a state block.
- **Restoring the turn origin in `mapSessionEvents`**, which would fix the transcript too. Left alone here: it changes protocol-level state well outside this bug, and that layer deliberately avoids content sniffing.

The underlying cause is worth a separate look: `_startAgentMergePrompt` marks these turns `MessageKind.SystemNotification`, but `mapSessionEvents` rebuilds them from the SDK log as plain user turns, so the transcript's compact merge widget also stops rendering after a restore.
